mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV engine typically costs £2,800-£5,500 supply-only, depending on the supplier and whether the hybrid system components are included. Used units start from £1,800. Supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 labour due to high-voltage system complexity. Main dealer replacement can exceed £8,000-£10,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV problems are high-voltage battery degradation reducing electric range (reported from 41 miles down to 17 miles in cold weather), onboard charger faults preventing plug-in charging, electric motor/inverter cooling system leaks, and timing chain tensioner wear on the EP6FDT petrol engine. The 1.6 hybrid is generally considered reliable - 'the most reliable engine Peugeot have made in a while' - but the hybrid system has its own failure points.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the hybrid engine on a Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound. A rebuilt unit costs £2,800-£5,500 versus £18,000-£35,000 for a comparable used 308 Hybrid 225. With dealer replacement potentially exceeding £8,000-£10,000, specialist rebuilt units offer significant savings. Hybrid vehicles command strong residuals, making replacement a sensible investment for well-maintained examples.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV battery last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV battery typically lasts 8-10 years or 80,000-120,000 miles. The 12.44 kWh battery is sensitive to temperature - owners report reduced range in cold weather (from 41 miles to as low as 17 miles). Battery health checks should be performed regularly. Extended warranty is recommended when buying used.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 and Hybrid 180?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 308 Hybrid 225 uses the EP6FDT 1.6L turbo petrol engine producing 180hp combined with an 81kW electric motor for 225hp total. The Hybrid 180 uses a 1.2L PureTech petrol engine producing 150hp combined. Both have similar electric-only range and battery capacity, but the 225 offers significantly more power. The 225 uses a timing chain (more reliable than the 1.2's wet belt). The 225 is also more expensive to replace.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV engine code is EP6FDT. It appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV is the plug-in hybrid flagship of the third-generation (Phase 3, 2021-present) 308 range, combining a 1.6-litre turbocharged petrol engine with a powerful electric motor for a combined 225hp output. The EP6FDT petrol engine - part of the Prince family jointly developed with BMW - delivers 180hp on its own, while the 81kW electric motor adds instant torque for seamless acceleration and up to 59 km (37 miles) of electric-only range. Paired with an 8-speed e-EAT8 automatic gearbox, the Hybrid 225 offers 0-62mph in 7.6 seconds and CO2 emissions from 26 g/km. The 1.6 Hybrid is considered one of the most reliable engines Peugeot has produced in recent years, using a timing chain rather than the wet belt found on smaller PureTech units.

milestones.description: **2021** - Third-generation 308 launched with EP6FDT 1.6 Hybrid 225 PHEV for GT and GT Pack trims
**2022** - Hybrid 225 carries over with minor ECU refinements and updated infotainment
**2023** - Battery management system updates to improve cold-weather range performance
**2024** - Continued production; 308 Hybrid 225 remains the performance PHEV option
**2025** - New generation of PHEV powertrains announced, but EP6FDT remains in service

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every EP6FDT engine fitted to the Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV's EP6FDT engine is considered one of the most reliable petrol units Peugeot has produced in recent years - using a timing chain rather than the wet belt found on smaller PureTech engines. However, the complexity of the plug-in hybrid system introduces its own failure points: battery degradation, onboard charger faults, and electric motor/inverter issues. Early production examples also saw a handful of traction chain and charger failures. Every rebuilt Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty - with specialist high-voltage system integration and calibration included.

problems.h4: High-Voltage Battery Degradation - Why Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV Engines Lose Electric Range
problems.rootCause: The 12.44 kWh lithium-ion battery pack degrades over time, reducing electric-only range. Owners have reported range dropping from 41 miles to as low as 17 miles in cold weather, though dealers often attribute this to temperature. Battery management system (BMS) faults can also trigger system warnings and reduced power output. Unlike some newer PHEVs, the 308 Hybrid does not use LFP battery technology.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of degraded battery modules, BMS recalibration

problems.recommendation: Battery degradation is the most common issue on the Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV. If you notice reduced electric-only range, have the battery health checked immediately. Extended warranty can be valuable - some owners recommend purchasing warranty extension when buying new or approved used. If the battery has lost more than 30% of its capacity, a replacement is usually more cost-effective than continued use. A rebuilt hybrid powertrain with a new battery pack is the most reliable long-term solution.

problems.h4: Onboard Charger & Charging Port Faults - Why Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV Systems Fail to Charge
problems.rootCause: The onboard charger and charging port can develop faults, preventing plug-in charging. Early production examples saw a handful of onboard charger failures. The standard charger is 3.6kW, with a 7.4kW optional upgrade available. Faults can also occur in the charging port or the cable itself.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of charging port or cable, system reset
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if fault is in the port or cable

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of onboard charger module, system recalibration
repairOptions.longevity: Restores charging function; requires specialist high-voltage handling

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new charger, battery and motor, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if charger fault has caused wider electrical system damage

problems.recommendation: Onboard charger faults on the Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV should be addressed promptly - without the ability to charge, the vehicle becomes a heavier, less efficient petrol car. Check that your vehicle has had any outstanding campaigns addressed. If the charger has failed, replacement is straightforward for a specialist. A full powertrain replacement is only necessary if the fault has caused wider electrical damage.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV powertrain prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain & Petrol Engine Wear - Why EP6FDT Units Develop Rattle and Loss of Power
problems.rootCause: The EP6FDT shares the Prince engine family's timing chain architecture - chain-driven, not wet belt. While more reliable than wet belt units, the timing chain tensioner can still wear over time, causing cold-start rattle and, in severe cases, chain jump. The 1.6 hybrid is considered the most reliable engine Peugeot has made in a while, but high-mileage examples may still develop chain issues. Carbon buildup on intake valves from direct injection is also a concern, though less severe than on earlier Prince engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of chain, tensioner (revised), guides and VANOS sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with upgraded timing components, new HPFP and hybrid system calibration, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped or caused valve damage

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV exhibits cold-start rattle, address it immediately - the 1.6 hybrid is reliable but timing chain issues can still occur on high-mileage examples. A timing chain kit replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Regular oil changes with correct 0W-30 fully synthetic oil are critical to preventing timing chain guide wear. Carbon cleaning every 60,000 miles is also recommended for direct-injection engines.

problems.group: Electric Motor & Inverter Cooling System Leaks
problems.h4: Electric Motor & Inverter Cooling System Leaks - Why Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV Systems Overheat
problems.rootCause: The electric motor and inverter have dedicated cooling systems that can develop leaks, leading to overheating and reduced power output. The 81kW (110hp) electric motor integrated with the e-EAT8 gearbox generates significant heat under load. Coolant leaks in the inverter cooling circuit can trigger system warnings and limit electric-only operation.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of coolant hoses, pump, or radiator; system flush and refill
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before motor/inverter damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new motor, inverter and cooling system, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if overheating has caused motor or inverter failure

problems.recommendation: Cooling system leaks on the Peugeot 308 Hybrid 225 PHEV should be addressed immediately. If you notice coolant loss or system warnings, have the cooling system inspected. Replacing hoses or the water pump early can prevent catastrophic motor or inverter failure. A full powertrain replacement is only necessary if overheating has caused internal damage.
